notes: Num 17:1 in the English Bible is 17:16 in the Hebrew text (BHS). See also the note on 16:36.

verses.zh: 「你晓谕以色列人，从他们手下取杖，每支派一根；从他们所有的首领，按着支派，共取十二根。你要将各人的名字写在各人的杖上，
verses.en: “Speak to the Israelites, and receive from them a staff from each tribe,[NOTE:1] one from every tribal leader,[NOTE:2] twelve staffs; you must write each man’s name on his staff.
notes: Heb “receive from them a rod, a rod from the house of a father.”
Heb “from every leader of them according to their fathers’ house.”
verses.commentary:
17:2 "a rod" This NOUN (BDB 641) has a wide semantic field.

- a staff

- walking staff (symbol of wealth and status as family leader) ‒ Gen. 38:18

(1) Moses' staff ‒ Exod. 4:2,17,20; 7:2,20; 14:16

(2) Aaron's staff ‒ Exod. 7:9,10,12,19, etc.

(3) court magician's staff ‒ Exod. 7:8-12

(4) God's staff ‒ Exod. 4:20; 17:9

- shepherd's staff

- symbol of sustaining food ‒ Lev. 20:26

- a rod

- a weapon ‒ 1 Sam. 14:27

- pole of tribe ‒ here

- symbol of power/rule ‒ Isa. 9:4; 10:5; 30:32

- symbol of wicked power ‒ Ezek. 7:11

- symbol of God's discipline ‒ Job 9:34; 21:9; Ps. 89:32

- a tribe (i.e., led by one with a leader's staff) ‒ Exod. 31:2; Lev. 24:11; Num. 1:4; Josh. 7:1; Mic. 6:9

- branch ‒ Ezek. 19:11,12,14 (twice); see JB; NJB has "branch" in Num. 17:2

The familiar passage in Ps. 23:4 has different but overlapping meanings.

- rod ‒ BDB 986

- staff ‒ BDB 1044

verses.zh: 并要将亚伦的名字写在利未的杖上，因为各族长必有一根杖。
verses.en: You must write Aaron’s name on the staff of Levi; for one staff is for the head of every tribe.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “one rod for the head of their fathers’ house.”

verses.zh: 你要把这些杖存在会幕内法柜前，就是我与你们相会之处。
verses.en: You must place them[NOTE:1] in the tent of meeting before the ark of the covenant[NOTE:2] where I meet with you.
notes: The verb is the Hiphil perfect of נוּחַ (nuakh, “to rest”), and so “to set at rest, lay, place, put.” The form with the vav (ו) consecutive continues the instruction of the previous verse.
The Hebrew text simply reads “the covenant” or “the testimony.”
verses.commentary:
17:4 "where I meet with you" This phrase shows the uniqueness of Moses' relationship with YHWH (and,
by implication, Aaron, cf. Exod. 4:10-16). The issue of YHWH's choice of Moses has already been made!

This rod blooming, like so many visible symbols (cf. v. 10; Num. 16:37-40) of YHWH's presence,
power, and purposes, will clearly reveal who is the leader of Israel (v. 5).

verses.zh: 后来我所拣选的那人，他的杖必发芽。这样，我必使以色列人向你们所发的怨言止息，不再达到我耳中。」
verses.en: And the staff of the man whom I choose will blossom; so I will rid myself of the complaints of the Israelites, which they murmur against you.”

verses.zh: 于是摩西晓谕以色列人，他们的首领就把杖交给他，按着支派，每首领一根，共有十二根；亚伦的杖也在其中。
verses.en: So Moses spoke to the Israelites, and each of their leaders gave him a staff, one for each leader,[NOTE:1] according to their tribes[NOTE:2]—twelve staffs; the staff of Aaron was among their staffs.
notes: Heb “a rod for one leader, a rod for one leader.”

verses.zh: 摩西就把杖存在法柜的帐幕内，在耶和华面前。
verses.en: Then Moses placed the staffs before the Lord in the tent of the testimony.[NOTE:1]
notes: The name of the tent now attests to the centrality of the ark of the covenant. Instead of the “tent of meeting” (מוֹעֵד, moʿed) we now find the “the tent of the testimony” (הָעֵדֻת, haʿedut).

verses.zh: 第二天，摩西进法柜的帐幕去。谁知利未族亚伦的杖已经发了芽，生了花苞，开了花，结了熟杏。
verses.en: On the next day Moses went into the tent of the testimony—and[NOTE:1] the staff of Aaron for the house of Levi had sprouted, and brought forth buds, and produced blossoms, and yielded almonds![NOTE:2]
notes: Here too the deictic particle (“and behold”) is added to draw attention to the sight in a vivid way.

There is no clear answer why the tribe of Levi had used an almond staff. The almond tree is one of the first to bud in the spring, and its white blossoms are a beautiful sign that winter is over. Its name became a name for “watcher”; Jeremiah plays on this name for God’s watching over his people (1:11-12).
verses.commentary:
17:8 This verse implies Aaron's rod showed a process of fruitfulness.

- sprouted ‒ BDB 827 I, KB 965, Qal PERFECT

- put forth buds ‒ BDB 422, KB 425, Hiphil IMPERFECT with waw

- blossomed ‒ BDB 847, KB 1013, Hiphil IMPERFECT with waw

- produced fruit ‒ BDB 168, KB 19, Qal IMPERFECT with waw

17:8-11 The tribes of Israel (i.e., their leaders) clearly saw and confirmed YHWH's choice.

verses.zh: 摩西就把所有的杖从耶和华面前拿出来，给以色列众人看；他们看见了，各首领就把自己的杖拿去。
verses.en: So Moses brought out all the staffs from before the Lord to all the Israelites. They looked at them,[NOTE:1] and each man took his staff.
notes: The words “at them” are not in the Hebrew text, but they have been added in the translation for clarity.

verses.zh: 耶和华吩咐摩西说：「把亚伦的杖还放在法柜前，给这些背叛之子留作记号。这样，你就使他们向我发的怨言止息，免得他们死亡。」
verses.en: The Lord said to Moses, “Bring Aaron’s staff back before the testimony to be preserved for a sign to the rebels, so that you may bring their murmurings to an end[NOTE:1] before me, that they will not die.”[NOTE:2]
notes: The verb means “to finish; to complete” and here “to bring to an end.” It is the imperfect following the imperative, and so introduces a purpose clause (as a final imperfect).
This is another final imperfect in a purpose clause.
verses.commentary:
17:10 YHWH wants Israel's past faithlessness to be a current warning. He does not want to judge His people.

▣ "rebels" This is literally the idiom "sons of rebellion" (BDB 598).

verses.zh: 摩西就这样行。耶和华怎样吩咐他，他就怎样行了。
verses.en: So Moses did as the Lord commanded him—this is what he did.
verses.commentary:
17:11 The theme of "obedience" is crucial in Numbers. See
SPECIAL TOPIC: KEEP.

verses.zh: 以色列人对摩西说：「我们死啦！我们灭亡啦！都灭亡啦！
verses.en: The Israelites said to Moses, “We are bound to die![NOTE:1] We perish, we all perish!
notes: The use of הֵן (hen) and the perfect tense in the nuance of a prophetic perfect expresses their conviction that they were bound to die—it was certain (see GKC 312-13 §106.n).
verses.commentary:
17:12-13 These verses seem out of place. They do not fit the flow of the context. There have been several theories.

- The Oxford Study Bible, p. 159, suggests they should go after Num. 14:34 (so too, JB)

- also possibly after Num. 14:41-45

- They represent the repentance of Israel after questioning YHWH's chosen leaders 3 times. They finally see the need
of an intermediating priesthood.

- It is an introduction to chapter 18.

Plagues were often a divine judgment on Israel, Num. 14:37; 16:45-50; 25:8-9, 18; 31:16; 2 Sam. 24:21, 28;
1 Chr. 21:22; 2 Chr. 21:14-15; Ps. 106:28-31; Jer. 21:6. But, note the purpose was always a purification resulting in repentance
and restoration of fellowship and covenant.

interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation.

These discussion questions are provided to help you think through the major issues of this section of
the book. They are meant to be thought-provoking, not definitive.

- Why does the Hebrew word "rod" also denote a tribe?

- If there are 13 tribes, why twelve rods?

- Why did God want Aaron's rod kept permanently?

- What is the contextual purpose of Num. 17:12-13?

verses.zh: 凡挨近耶和华帐幕的是必死的。我们都要死亡吗？」
verses.en: (17:28)[NOTE:1] Anyone who even comes close to the tabernacle of the Lord will die! Are we all to die?”[NOTE:2]
notes: Num 17:13 in the English Bible is 17:28 in the Hebrew text (BHS). See also the note on 16:36.
The verse stresses the completeness of their death: “will we be consumed by dying” (הַאִם תַּמְנוּ לִגְוֹעַ, haʾim tamnu ligvoaʿ).
